comment: Static IL patches applied to the player's sts2.dll by Spire.Patcher (tools/build_logic.py). Each replaces a Harmony patch from sts2-cli; handlers for 'redirect' ids are in logic/Spire.Logic/Hooks.cs. A missing non-optional target fails the build: that is the signal the game API moved (see docs/LOGIC_BUILD.md).

patches.note: Cuts the game logic off from its Godot UI layer: every call from logic into a UI class (namespace MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Nodes.*, or any game class deriving from a Godot class, e.g. NDebugAudioManager) becomes a recorded presentation cue (sound, VFX, speech, music) with a safe default result. A singleton getter (NCombatRoom.Instance) heading a ?. chain that is a statement of its own returns a stand-in instead of null, so calls such as Instance?.PlaySplashVfx(...) or Instance?.CombatVfxContainer.AddChildSafely(NThinSliceVfx.Create(...)) are recorded rather than skipped; chains that dereference or keep a UI result outside the UI keep the null (Spire.Patcher IsStatementUiChain).

The Godot UI layer never runs headless (the 'ui' patch redirects every call into it). Method bodies of the Godot-derived classes there (nodes, and what is nested in them) become a throw so the AOT builds do not compile the UI (console code size). Constructors stay, and plain helper classes in those namespaces (EpochComparer) are untouched. A 'headless: ...' NotSupportedException in a log means the logic reached UI code.

Game logic calls into Godot engine objects (scenes from the asset cache, tweens, nodes) that are null without the engine. A null receiver now skips the call with a safe default; non-null receivers (stub objects) behave as before.
Game code awaits Task.Delay for pacing (e.g. Amalgamator). A real timer would leave the adapter reporting a decision mid-effect; every call completes at once and records a 'wait' cue instead.

CardCmd.Preview(card(s), time, style): the cards shown in NRun.GlobalUi's preview container, then flown to their pile; these return before the UI in TestMode. Recorded as deck_card show cues outside combat.
CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd(result(s), time, style): the cards just added, shown and flown to their pile. Recorded as deck_card add cues outside combat.
CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck(cards, showPreview): the card grows in and burns away (NCardRemoveVfx). Recorded as deck_card remove cues.
CardCmd.Upgrade(cards, style): its preview style, for the deck cards it upgrades (deck.upgraded).
The end of CardCmd.Upgrade(cards, style).
A card upgraded inside CardCmd.Upgrade: a deck card gets NCardUpgradeVfx in the style's container. Recorded as a deck_card upgrade cue.
CardCmd.Transform(transformations, rng, style): its preview style (the transformations are not enumerated here).
Transform's original card, just before AfterTransformedTo on its replacement.
Transform's replacement: in the deck, NCardTransformVfx (original to replacement) in the style's container. Recorded as a deck_card transform cue.
TheArchitect.OnRoomEnter finds the Architect among the room's creature nodes (none headless); the hook gives it the layout combat's enemy, so its lines, attacks (and their RNG) run as in the game.
PlayCurrentLine's first line: the head stops reading, then looks normal (track 1). Recorded as an anim cue.

AnimPlayerAttackIfNecessary's hits: NDamageNumVfx.Create(ArchitectCreature, part, false) and NHitSparkVfx go into NCombatRoom's VFX container, which is null headless (their arguments are never made). The parts are recorded with each hit's VfxCmd.PlayOnCreatureCenter.
NEventRoom.Instance?.VfxContainer?.AddChildSafely(NMirrorVfx.Create()): the container is null headless, so Create never runs. Recorded as its ui cue.
NEventRoom's VfxContainer gets NRainVfx.Create() (as the mirror). Recorded as its ui cue.
Trial.Accept: RemoveNodesOnPortrait, the accused's VFX on the portrait at (292, 68), SetPortrait(trial_started). The node and texture do not exist headless; recorded as an event_portrait cue.

The Sovereign Blade orbiting the player is a node the game finds under the creature (SovereignBlade.GetVfxNode); headless there is none, so every forge looked like a new blade. The adapter keeps which blades exist and records blade cues (forge, orbit) with the forge / refine sound.
The play's target, for the blade's attack (blade.attack_node).
SovereignBlade.OnPlay's BeforeDamage: the blade (vfxNode.Attack) flies at the target. Recorded as a blade attack cue; the call still finds no node.
The blade goes (RemoveSovereignBlade: exhausted, transformed). Recorded as a blade remove cue.

The adapter runs the game with TestMode on, and some rules depend on it: a new profile's first act is an undiscovered alternate act (ActModel.GetRandomList), shop potion prices vary by +/-5% (MerchantPotionEntry, a Shops RNG draw), bosses and encounters follow the discovery order and a first run's unknown rooms are events (RunManager's tutorial rules), the run history records HP and gold per floor and reloads are counted. Runs that follow the game's own flow (start_game_run) see TestMode off at exactly these sites; other runs see the real value, unchanged.
See testmode.game_flow.is_off.

Presentation the game skips in TestMode, with no effect on the rules: the potion thrown from the player to its target (NItemThrowVfx, then a 0.5 s wait), the rest site's healing cross, and the monsters' calls on their special nodes (the Myte's and Snapping Jaxfruit's targets, the Flyconid's spore kind). TestMode reads off there in every run, so it reaches the steps as cues (the UI calls stay redirected).

DecimillipedeSegment.AnimSegmentsAttack plays its rocks the way VfxCmd.PlayFullScreenInCombat does (the scene at the screen's centre in the combat VFX container), written out in the move. The scene lookup becomes the same 'vfx at screen' cue; it returns null as the asset cache does headless.

Creature.GetCreatureNode returns null in TestMode; in every run here it reaches the UI stand-ins (NCombatRoom.GetCreatureNode, NBestiary.GetCreatureNode), so the monsters' calls on their creature nodes become cues. DecimillipedeSegment.AnimSegmentsAttack: the segments' AttackShake (special nodes) and the rocks scene (its asset is null headless, so nothing is made in the logic) before a 0.5 s wait. Presentation only: the nodes are stand-ins whose calls are redirected.
Records how the run ended (RunManager.OnEnded: progress, history, epochs). WinRun calls it at the end of The Architect and then kills the player, so the adapter needs the outcome to report a victory.
